messages:
Kai: RFC follow-up — I sketched a lightweight approach for long-term modularization: introduce an "ownership anchoring" pattern + thin "stitch adapters" to separate hotpath runtime from control-plane concerns. Short bullets below, looking for quick buy-in.

Rebecca: quick Q — what exactly do you mean by "ownership anchoring"?

Kai: by anchoring we mean "explicit service ownership for a capability boundary" (eg: kv-cache, session-routing, prefix-caching). Each anchor owns state + migration contract; adapters talk to anchors over a strict shim.

Sam: love the intent. main tradeoff is extra network hop vs faster team autonomy. are we planning colocated adapters or remote RPC?

Kai: colocation for latency-critical slices (hotpath), remote adapters for admin/observability flows. key is small stable wire contract.

Morgan: rollout checklist idea: 1) define anchor contract 2) implement shim adapter + health hooks 3) canary traffic split 4) rollback plan + data compatibility tests.

ArchBot: Created GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/4212 — "ownership-anchors + stitch adapters — implementation spike"

Rebecca: sample contract? can you paste a minimal interface so infra can eval perf impact.

Kai: sure — minimal shim (pseudo):
```
interface StitchAdapter {
  get(session_id: string): SessionState | null
  update(session_id: string, delta: Partial<SessionState>): bool
  stats(): AdapterMetrics
}
```
Contract notes: strictly typed payloads, stable fields only; adapters must support a TTL-aware read path for prefix cache.

Sam: on data migration: how do we handle existing KV caches when an anchor takes ownership? snapshot + dual-read?

Kai: plan is dual-read for N minutes + background reconciliation. fallback if divergence > X%. Also version-tagged keys during transition.

Morgan: monitoring: we'll need per-anchor SLOs and automatic degradation signals. Suggest alerts on 95p latency, error rate, and cache divergence metric.

Rebecca: can we implement a soft-fallback in adapter to route to a compatible legacy path if adapter health degraded? avoids hard cutovers.

Kai: yes — adapters must implement fallback policy. Example config: 
```
adapter.config = {
  fallback: {enabled: true, threshold_ms: 150, error_rate: 0.02},
  canary_pct: 5
}
```

Sam: metrics + tracing needs — ensure span tags include anchor_id and adapter_version for rollbacks.

ArchBot: FYI: linked infra perf test plan in issue 4212, and added a perf job: perf/anchor-smoke.

Morgan: action items: @Rebecca proto for contract (due EOD Wed), @Sam migration runbook draft (due Fri), Kai to implement adapter PoC and perf baseline (next week). I'll add telemetry dashboard templates.

Rebecca: ack, starting proto now.

Sam: ack, will draft migration steps and dual-read harness.

Kai: thanks. If no objections I'll post the RFC follow-up doc with the contract and rollout checklist by EOD. Short, iterative cutovers only — we avoid big-bang. :thumbsup:

Morgan: agreed. small slices + clear rollback = win. :rocket:
